proof:
# Affine scale: an exact obstruction to a factor-two continuous minorant

This tests a proposed extension of the constant-scale one-integer proof.
It retains a canonical convex body, positive sampled fibers, one integer
coordinate, a full homothetic envelope plateau with an interior integer
witness, and no fiber carrying half the total original volume.

It does NOT assert that the plateau consists of actual global deepest
sources or that a specified cap menu is an actual H-critical menu.
Therefore it does not refute an H-specific theorem using those additional
constraints. It refutes the geometric quadrature/large-fiber dichotomy
stated below.

## 1. Exact compatible family

Fix d>=2 and any convex d-body D containing 0 in its interior. Let

    ell(z)=z+1,    0<=z<=3,
    r(z)=z+1 for 0<=z<=2,    r(z)=3 for 2<=z<=3,
    C={(z,x):0<=z<=3, x in r(z)D}.

The positive function r is concave. Convexity of D and Minkowski
addition of homothetic copies show that C is convex. It is compact with
ambient interior. Since r is affine on every interval between
consecutive integers, C is exactly the canonical hull of the four
sampled fibers

    K_0=D, K_1=2D, K_2=3D, K_3=3D.

The sampled base P={0,1,2,3} is complete and every fiber is positive.
The affine envelope ell(z)D contains every actual real fiber and is
equal to it throughout B=[0,2], whose integer relative-interior witness
is 1. The envelope scale has the global positive floor 1.

Writing V=|D|, the original masses are

    V, 2^d V, 3^d V, 3^d V,
    M=(1+2^d+2*3^d)V.

Thus every sampled fiber has mass strictly less than M/2.

## 2. The pointed density has a jump exceeding two

Let p_D be the Minkowski gauge and put xi=x/ell(z).
At the four integer bases the pointed fibers are

    D_0=D_1=D_2=D,          D_3=(3/4)D.

The original mixed volume in pointed coordinates has density

    f(xi)=S 1_D(xi)+4^d 1_((3/4)D)(xi),
    S=1+2^d+3^d.                                      (1)

Indeed the Jacobian of the own-fiber coordinate change is ell(z)^d.
For d>=2,

    4^d>1+2^d+3^d=S.                                  (2)

At d=2 this is 16>14. After division by 4^d the three terms on the
right strictly decrease as d increases, proving all higher cases.

There is NO positive continuous function g on int(D) satisfying

    f/2<=g<=f almost everywhere.                        (3)

To prove this, choose any point xi_0 on the boundary of (3/4)D.
It lies in int(D). Approach it from the interior and from the exterior
of (3/4)D while remaining in int(D). Both approach regions contain
positive-volume open sets. Continuity and the almost-everywhere bounds
force simultaneously

    g(xi_0)>=(S+4^d)/2,       g(xi_0)<=S,

contrary to (2).

In particular no bounded positive log-concave density with full convex
support D can obey (3), because it is continuous on int(D). The same
holds for a positive density whose inverse power is finite convex.
Boundary redefinitions and null-set exceptions cannot repair the gap.

## 3. The natural weighted quadrature also fails explicitly

For a pointed xi with t=p_D(xi), its actual base occupancy interval is

    A_xi=[0,min(3,3/t-1)]

when 0<t<=1, with the obvious full interval at t=0.
On the open annulus 3/4<t<1 this interval contains exactly 0,1,2, and
the natural continuous weighted filling is

    G(xi)=integral_(A_xi) ell(z)^d dz
         =[(3/t)^(d+1)-1]/(d+1).                      (4)

As t ranges across that annulus, its limiting maximum/minimum ratio is

    [4^(d+1)-1]/[3^(d+1)-1]>2.                         (5)

Since f=S there, no constant c>0 can satisfy f/2<=cG<=f even almost
everywhere. Formula (3) is stronger: changing this particular filling
to any continuous minorant does not solve the issue.

## 4. Exact scope and the remaining possible dichotomy

The following proposed auxiliary assertion is false:

    For one integer coordinate and a positive affine envelope scale,
    compatible fibers with an occupied full homothetic source-shaped
    plateau either have a half-mass fiber, or their pointed density
    has a continuous factor-two minorant of the radial-centering class.

The example satisfies the geometric premises and violates both
conclusions. Calling B an actual deepest-source plateau would add a
substantial premise not verified here.

Indeed all the actual fibers in this example are homothetic copies of
D with affine centroid graph. Their OC bound follows by the elementary
weighted-base-center argument; the example is not an OC counterexample.
Any valid extension of the new H argument must use its actual
deepestness/quantile equations, a different affine-scale decomposition,
or a branch beyond the simple largest-fiber and pointwise-minorant
alternatives.
